setup: Why did the challah go to therapy?
punchline: It had too many twists in its life.

setup: What does a bagel say before breakfast?
punchline: Let’s get this schmear started.

setup: Why was the matzah so calm?
punchline: Nothing could get a rise out of it.

setup: Why did the kugel win an award?
punchline: It was outstanding in its dish.

setup: What did one latke say to the other?
punchline: You look a little fried.

setup: Why did the menorah feel confident?
punchline: It knew how to light up a room.

setup: Why did the bagel apply for a job?
punchline: It wanted to bring home the lox.

setup: What is a Jewish grandmother’s favorite exercise?
punchline: Reaching across the table to give you more food.

setup: A rabbi orders tea. The waiter asks, “Anything else?”
punchline: The rabbi says, “A little peace and quiet would be a miracle.”

setup: The brisket said, “I need more time.” What did Grandma say?
punchline: “Finally, someone who understands me.”

setup: Why did the gefilte fish bring a suitcase?
punchline: It was ready to take the plunge.

setup: Why did the rabbi carry a pencil?
punchline: In case he needed to draw a conclusion.

setup: What did the pickle say at the family dinner?
punchline: I’m kind of a big dill around here.

setup: Why did Grandma bring a ladder to lunch?
punchline: She heard the soup was on the house.

setup: Why was the synagogue clock always relaxed?
punchline: It knew everything would happen in good time.

setup: What did the blintz say after a compliment?
punchline: You’re making me flip.

setup: Why did the noodle call its mother?
punchline: It was feeling a little twisted.

setup: Why did the rabbi sit near the bakery?
punchline: He wanted a little spiritual nourishment.

setup: What did Grandma say when the family arrived early?
punchline: “Who are you, and what have you done with my relatives?”

setup: Why did the dreidel refuse to argue?
punchline: It didn’t want things to spin out of control.

setup: What is the fastest thing at a holiday dinner?
punchline: The phrase, “Have another helping.”

setup: Why did the bagel take a vacation?
punchline: It needed time to unwind.

setup: Why was the soup invited to every gathering?
punchline: It always brought warmth to the table.

setup: What did Grandma say to the empty plate?
punchline: “Don’t worry, I can fix that.”

setup: Why did the matzah read the newspaper?
punchline: It wanted the whole story, flat out.

setup: Why did the cantor bring an umbrella?
punchline: The forecast called for high notes.

setup: What did the kugel say after dinner?
punchline: That was grate.

setup: Why did the family recipe refuse to retire?
punchline: It still had plenty of thyme.

setup: Why did Grandma keep a spare chair at the table?
punchline: Because somebody is always bringing somebody.

setup: Why did the challah cross the road?
punchline: To prove it wasn’t just another roll.
